Heilprin repeats the chain in the Acha entry, with several cited episodes. Chagigah 19b gives Acha bar Adda but not this chain in the checked passage. The other exact attribution still needs a direct locus.
The named teacher and which Hamnuna he instructed remain Heilprin’s reconstruction. Kiddushin 29b records direct contact; Tosafot separates the men through its own argument.
The exact Eruvin chain as phrased remains open. The reference to Hadar does give Hamnuna in the time of Chisda and a distinction made by Tosafot.
The Zeira variant and the N.Y. siglum remain unresolved independently. Zevachim 105b verifies the following dialogue. Menachot 17a supplies a separate use of the comparable verb in the Chanina chain.
The digital halakhah numbering differs from Heilprin’s locator. The exact attribution appears at Kilayim 4:2 and has an additional parallel in Jerusalem Sukkah.
The exact Yerushalmi location remains open. The Tavi entry names the first halakhah of Lulav HaGazul. The checked chapter opening did not supply the exact form.
The exact direct transmission still needs a witness. The checked Gittin parallel has Yaakov and Hamnuna’s son in an Adda chain.
The exact Beer Sheva passage remains open. The direct digital commentary on Horayot 14a was read and did not contain the reported line. The adjacent index did not yield a source.
The student-colleague status is Heilprin’s reading of the form of address and parallel reports. Berakhot has Chisda address Hamnuna as master; Tosafot discusses a student figure elsewhere.
The checked folio 84 does not give the described address. Eruvin 54a expressly has Rav addressing Hamnuna. Keep the printed additional locator visible.
The exact local siglum stays visible. The context most naturally concerns the two Hamnunas, but the written same initials can also denote Rav Huna.
The exact Arukh geographical wording remains open. Rashi directly gives a town and a cave at Charta deArgaz. The cited Rashi in Berakhot attests Baghdad’s prominence, a separate proposition.
The precise travel passage remains unlocated. The nearby Heilprin and Rashi geography does not establish that Benjamin describes the same place.
The source siglum and Kefar Alma burial tradition remain open. Heilprin’s alternative location stands alongside the Bavli transfer and Rashi’s Charta deArgaz report.
The regional burial inference remains Heilprin’s. The named cave and the transfer story are directly located. Their historical relationships remain unestablished.
